chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Nuhayki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Three [groups of people] will be under the Shade of the Throne of God on the Day when there is no shade except His Shade: a man who marries off his Muslim brother, or serves him, or keeps a secret for him.
ai.seo_question: What are the three deeds that earn the Shade of God's Throne on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) to emphasize that social cohesion through marriage facilitation, mutual service, and secret-keeping are not merely social niceties but acts of worship that secure divine proximity. These three acts reflect the Shia emphasis on 'al-wala' wal-barra' (affection and loyalty) within the community, transforming interpersonal bonds into spiritual shields on the Day of Judgment. The 'Shade of the Throne' signifies a unique state of comfort and protection from the terror of resurrection, reserved for those who actively nurture the spiritual and social fabric of the Ummah.
